messages:
sam: Heads up — running into 401s from our SDK in GitLab CI. Token works locally but fails on the runner. Error looked like Basic auth rejected. Anyone seen this?

anya: Yup. Often it's a trailing newline or CRLF from copying the key into the CI variable. Runners will send the raw string.

raj: Quick checks: what does your Authorization header look like? If you're doing Basic, remember it should be base64 of "<apiKey>:" (note the colon even if password empty).

sam: I was doing this in the job: `export API_KEY="$CI_JOB_TOKEN"` then `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo $API_KEY | base64)" ...` — I guess echo adds a newline.

anya: yep — `echo` adds a trailing newline. Use `echo -n` or better `printf '%s' "$API_KEY"`. Example: `Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$API_KEY:" | base64)` (colon included).

raj: If you're on Alpine / busybox `echo -n` is ok, but POSIX-safe is `printf`. Also for base64 with no wraps: `printf '%s' "$API_KEY:" | base64 | tr -d '\n'` or on GNU coreutils `base64 -w0`.

marco: For Go folks: use `req.SetBasicAuth(apiKey, "")` — that will include the colon and do the correct base64 encoding for you. Avoid hand-rolling unless you know exactly what you're encoding.

sam: Nice. We're using a small custom client, so we were assembling header manually and forgot the colon. That explains it.

anya: Also watch Windows-style newlines if the secret was copied from a Windows host: `tr -d '\r'` or `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tr -d '\r'` before encoding. GitLab masked vars sometimes preserve CR.

raj: PowerShell tip for those setting env in PS runner: `[System.Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$env:API_KEY:"))` — ensures no extra newline.

sam: For Kubernetes secrets: remember k8s expects base64-encoded values. Use `echo -n 'myval' | base64 -w0` (or `-n`/`printf`) so the secret doesn't get the newline baked in.

marco: One more gotcha — some SDKs or middleware may automatically trim whitespace from tokens, others do not. If your server expects the colon (username:password) and you pass a trimmed string without adding `:`, you'll auth-fail.

anya: TL;DR checklist: 1) ensure colon is present when forming Basic auth (`apiKey:`), 2) strip CR/LF before base64, 3) prefer language helpers (SetBasicAuth), 4) use `printf` or `echo -n` when building base64 on *nix, 5) PowerShell has different idioms.

sam: Thanks — fixed in CI by changing to `export API_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$CI_JOB_TOKEN" | tr -d '\r')` and building header with `printf '%s' "$API_KEY:" | base64 -w0`. Job now passes :tada:

dev-bot: Note added to #runbook: "CI: strip newlines from API keys before encoding for Basic auth"

marco: If anyone hits this in other repos, ping me — I can send a tiny helper script that normalizes tokens for jobs.

sam: Appreciate it. Closing this thread.
